'''George C. Prendergast''' (born 1961) is an American biomedical scientist. His research has focused on cancer pathobiology and immunology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/prendergast-george-c |title= George C. Prendergast - Science History |website= sciencehistory.org |access-date=12 November 2008}}</ref> Since 2004, he has been the president and CEO of [[Lankenau Institute for Medical Research]], a cancer-focused research center in the U.S.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mainlinehealth.org/research/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research/researchers/our-faculty/george-prendergast|title=Lankenau Institute for Medical Research - George C. Prendergast, PhD|access-date=29 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mainlinehealth.org/research/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research/about/our-history-and-accomplishments|title= Lankenau Institute for Medical Research: History and Accomplishments}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2011/06/110614115037.htm |title= Low-carbohydrate, high-protein diets may reduce both tumor growth rates and cancer risk |website= sciencedaily.com |access-date=15 June 2011}}</ref> He is also the co-director of the Program in Cancer Cell Biology & Signaling at the Sidney Kimmel Cancer Center, [[Thomas Jefferson University]].<ref name="KCC">[http://www.kimmelcancercenter.org/research/areas/basicscience/CellBiology.php Program in Cancer Cell Biology & Signaling, Kimmel Cancer Center, Thomas Jefferson University]</ref>

== Education ==
Prendergast earned his bachelor's degree in biochemistry from the [[University of Pennsylvania]], his master's degree in molecular biophysics and biochemistry from [[Yale University]] and his PhD in molecular biology from [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mainlinehealth.org/research/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research/researchers/our-faculty/george-prendergast|title=Resident Faculty of Lankenau Institute for Medical Research: George C. Prendergast, Ph.D.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/ltgnsjx|title=Science History Institute: Oral history interview with George C. Prendergast (2003)}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mainlinehealth.org/research/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research/technology-development-licensing|title=Lankenau Institute for Medical Research: Technology Development and Licensing}}</ref> He was later an [[American Cancer Society]] postdoctoral fellow at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute at [[New York University Medical Center]] before working in the Department of [[Cancer Research]] at Merck.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://go.myabcam.com/immunochemotherapy-the-future-of-cancer-treatment-webinar |title= Immunochemotherapy: The future of cancer treatment |website= myabcam.com |access-date=18 August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/philadelphia/news/2019/08/23/main-line-research-institute-turns-to-jefferson.html|title=Philadelphia Business Journal: Main Line research institute turns to Jefferson for invention licensing help}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1993, Prendergast joined the faculties of The Wistar Institute and the Department of Genetics at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. In 1999, he also became a senior director at the DuPont Pharmaceuticals Company.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.spandidos-publications.com/COVER_LEGENDS/ijo_31_2_cover_legend.pdf |title= Immunochemotherapy: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ONCOLOGY |website= spandidos-publications.com |access-date=31 March 2007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.biospace.com/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research-president-and-ceo-invited-to-speak-at-three-oncology-and-biotechnology-conferences-this-spring |title= Lankenau Institute for Medical Research President And CEO Invited To Speak At Three Oncology And Biotechnology Conferences This Spring |website= BioSpace |access-date=19 April 2016}}</ref>

In 2002, he moved his groups at Wistar and DuPont to the Lankenau Institute for Medical Research (LIMR) and became the president and CEO there in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.spandidos-publications.com/COVER_LEGENDS/ijo_31_2_cover_legend.pdf |title= Immunochemotherapy: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ONCOLOGY |website= spandidos-publications.com |access-date=31 March 2007}}</ref> At LIMR, Prendergast created an organizational model for nonprofit biomedical research termed the acapreneurial™ model, whose stated aim is to balance academic studies with invention, product development and partnered entrepreneurialism.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/183695/bio |title= Loop - George C. Prendergast |website= frontiersin.org |access-date=31 December 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/philadelphia/news/2019/08/23/main-line-research-institute-turns-to-jefferson.html|title=Philadelphia Business Journal: Main Line research institute turns to Jefferson for invention licensing help}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.biospace.com/lankenau-institute-for-medical-research-president-and-ceo-invited-to-speak-at-three-oncology-and-biotechnology-conferences-this-spring |title= Lankenau Institute for Medical Research President And CEO Invited To Speak At Three Oncology And Biotechnology Conferences This Spring |website= BioSpace |access-date=19 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/philadelphia/news/2020/01/30/guiding-light-main-line-startup-taps-lankenau.html |title= Guiding light: Main Line startup taps Lankenau Institute's glow tech to make antibodies |website= bizjournals.com |access-date=30 January 2001}}</ref>

Prendergast's current research focuses on new uses of IDO1 inhibitory drugs in medicine, investigations of the IDO2 enzyme in cancer and autoimmunity, and therapeutic antibodies that target the disease severity modifier genes Bin1 and RhoB to broadly treat autoimmune disorders and diabetic complications.

His research team pioneered the early discovery and development of experimental drugs that inhibit the tryptophan catabolizing enzyme IDO1 as a new type of oral immunotherapy for cancer,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/77/24/6795|title=Discovery of IDO1 Inhibitors: From Bench to Bedside|journal=Cancer Research|date=15 December 2017|volume=77|issue=24|pages=6795–6811|last1=Prendergast|first1=George C.|last2=Malachowski|first2=William P.|last3=Duhadaway|first3=James B.|last4=Muller|first4=Alexander J.|doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-17-2285|pmid=29247038|pmc=6021761}}</ref> currently under study worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i14/Using-IDO1-Inhibitors-Combat-Cancer.html|title=Journal of the National Cancer Institute: Using IDO1 Inhibitors To Combat Cancer}}</ref> 
 
In 2008, Prendergast was recognized as one of the 250 most influential alumni of [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/article/list|title=Princeton Alumni Weekly: The List|date=21 January 2016}}</ref> From 2010-2017, Prendergast was Editor-in-Chief of Cancer Research, a journal of the [[American Association for Cancer Research]], one of the most cited in the field.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://annualreport2017.aacr.org/scientific_publishing.html|title=American Association for Cancer Research 2017 Annual Report - Scientific Publishing}}</ref> In 2018, Prendergast was named The Havens Chair in Biomedical Research by the [[Lankenau Medical Center]] Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mainlinehealth.org/news/2017/05/09/havens-establish-endowed-chair-for-biomedical-research-at-lankenau|title=Main Line Health: Peter and Louise Havens establish endowed chair for biomedical research at Lankenau|date=9 May 2017}}</ref>
